sentences.text:
The Honourable Justice M.G. Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A. No.428 of 2020
Judgment:

This Appeal is filed by the claimant/injured aggrieved by the judgment and decree, dated 13.04.2016 made in M.V.O.P.No.431 of 2013 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad (for short, the Tribunal).

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, hereinafter, the parties are referred to as per their array before the Tribunal.

3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- (Rupees Six Lakhs) towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.08.2012.

As per the contents of the petition, on 12.08.2012 while the petitioner along with his wife, daughter were proceeding on Hero Honda motorcycle bearing No. AP.11.M.3720 from Nagireddipally to Thukkapuram village, the driver of Maruthi Car bearing No. AP.10.H.9115 drove the his car in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed and came in opposite direction and lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the vehicle of the petitioner at the outskirts of Tukkapuram village.
As a result, the petitioner, his wife and MGP, J Macma_428_2020 daughter fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries besides fractures.

The petitioner was shifted to Kamineni Hospital, Hyderabad, wherein he underwent treatment for open grade III B communited segmental fracture shaft right femur with bone loss,
open grade II B compound fracture both bones right leg with butter fragment, fracture lateral end of clavicle, fracture base of 5th metatarsal fight foot and undergone major surgeries for implants.

According to him, due to the accident, he was unable to attend his regular works as he sustained permanent disability and therefore, he filed the claim petition against the respondents seeking compensation under different heads.

4. Before the Tribunal, respondent Nos. 1 & 2, contested the claim denying the averments of the claim petition and contended that the amount claimed is excessive and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5.

Considering the claim, counter and the evidence, both oral and documentary placed on record,
the learned Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part by awarding compensation of Rs. 5,04,000/-.
The claimant preferred the present Appeal for enhancement of compensation.
MGP, J Macma_428_2020 6.

Heard Sri C. Mohan Prakash, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant and Sri A.V.K.S. Prasad,
Standing Counsel for the Respondent No. 2 / Insurance Company and perused the material T. Srisailam vs T. Kumar And Another on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174586997/

sentences.text:
7. Before going into the merits of the case, it is pertinent to note that though the claim is for Rs.6,00,000/-, during the pendency of this Appeal, the petitioner has filed I.A.No.1 of 2021 seeking amendment of claim from Rs.6,00,000/- to Rs.10,00,000/- and accordingly the said interlocutory application was allowed on 26.09.2023.
8.
The finding of the Tribunal with regard to the manner in which the accident took place has become final as the same is not challenged either by the owner or insurer of the vehicle.

9. The short question that arises for consideration in this appeal is "whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and equitable"?
10.

The learned counsel for the appellant-claimant contended that the claimant was working as Village Revenue Officer (VRO) and earning Rs.12,000/- per month and on account of accident he did not attend his office which is evident from oral evidence of PW1 MGP, J Macma_428_2020 and documentary evidence under Ex. A-6 loss of pay certificate.
However, the learned Tribunal has erred in taking the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month.

It is further contended that the claimant/injured has sustained multiple fractures to his right leg apart from other grievous injuries and that he underwent major surgeries and suffered 30% disability as per the evidence of P.W.2, the treating doctor, who also deposed that the claimant has suffered 30% disability which is partial and permanent in nature and issued the Disability Certificate as per Ex. A-8 and the learned Tribunal ought to have granted just compensation separately for functional disability and for permanent disability.

It is also contended that the learned Tribunal erroneously exonerated the respondent No.
2 - Insurance company on the sole ground that the driver of the crime vehicle is not having valid and subsisting driving licence as on the date of accident, which is contrary to the decision laid down by Honourable Supreme Court in Francisca Luiza Rocha and others v. K. Valarmathi and others.

entities.text: Francisca Luiza Rocha and others v. K. Valarmathi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 It is further contended that the learned Tribunal erred in not awarding any future prospects and even the amounts granted under the heads of pain & suffering; loss of earnings; transportation, 1 2018 ACJ 1430.

MGP, J Macma_428_2020 attendant charges and extra nourishment are meager and prayed for enhancement.
11.

On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that considering the nature of injuries and length of treatment, the Tribunal has adequately awarded the compensation and therefore, prayed for dismissal of the Appeal.

12. It is pertinent to note that the appellant/claimant has categorically stated in his evidence that he was working as Village Revenue Officer in Surepally Village of Bhongir Mandal, Nalgonda District.
However, the petitioner has not filed any documentary evidence to prove that he was working as Village Revenue Officer and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.

The learned Tribunal drawn a conclusion that in absence of any documentary proof either salary certificate or pay slips to establish the income of the petitioner, fixed his income as Rs.5,000/- per month.

2 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Although, the appellant/claimant has not filed any documentary proofs to establish his income,
he filed Loss of Pay certificate under Ex.A-6.

A perusal of Ex.A6 disclose that the Tahsildar, Bhongir Mandal has certified that from 12.08.2012 to 23.06.2013 the petitioner, who was working as Village Revenue MGP, J Macma_428_2020 Officer of Surepally village, availed medical leave.
Thus, Ex.A6 discloses that the appellant/petitioner was working as Village Revenue Officer during the relevant point of time.

This court, after considering the year of the accident and in absence of any salary or pay slip of the deceased and also by considering the statutory deductions from the gross salary of the petitioner/claimant, is inclined to consider the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.8,000/-,
which is appearing to be just and reasonable.
Thus, in view of the above discussion this court is of the opinion that the appellant/claimant monthly income can be taken as Rs.8,000/- per month.

14. Now, coming to the disability aspect, the learned Tribunal after considering the oral evidence of PW-2 Doctor, who treated the appellant and in view of Ex.A-8 Disability Certificate, has assessed the disability as 30% partial and permanent disability.

The learned Tribunal has rightly considered the above document while computing the compensation which seems to be just and reasonable, as such; there is no need to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal, so far as the percentage of disability is concerned.

15. Another contention of the learned counsel for appellant/claimant is that the disability in the case on hand has to MGP, J Macma_428_2020 be considered on separate footing on the basis of functional disability and for permanent disability, therefore, partial permanent disability should be 30% as assessed by PW-2 and functional disability as 100% and in support of his contention he relied upon the decision of Honourable Apex Court in Syed Sadiq v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited 2 and Rekha Jain v. National Insurance Company Limited 3.
16.

entities.text: Syed Sadiq v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rekha Jain v. National Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of Ex. A-8 disability certificate and evidence of PW- 2 categorically establishes that the disability is partial and permanent in nature and not for whole body.

It is settled principle that if disability is permanent in nature then the loss is to be assessed on the basis of functional disability resulting from medical disability and in case of temporary disability the injured is to be compensated for the loss of income for the period he could not work on account of such disability.
As evident from Ex. A-8 disability certificate, column no. 7 clearly states that disability is not functional in nature.

It is relevant to place reliance on the decision of Honorable Apex Court in the New India Assurance 2 2014 (2) SCC 735 3 2013 ACJ 2161 MGP, J Macma_428_2020 Company Limited V. Satish Chandra Sharma & Another, 4 wherein the Honourable Supreme Court reduced the compensation awarded by the High Court to a government servant considering that there was no permanent disability and that the claimant wasn't immobilized and continued to work even after the accident and that the claimant continued to earn the monthly salary he was earlier drawing,
including increments, except some allowances given due to nature of posting.

entities.text: New India Assurance 2 2014 (2) SCC 735 3 2013 ACJ 2161 MGP,

17. Further in case of T.J Parmeshwarappa and others v. The Branch manager, New India Assurance Company Limited and others 5 at Paragraph Nos. 8 and 9 the Honourable Court has elaborately discussed as to the yardsticks that needs to be considered while assessing award separately under functional and permanent disability, the relevant paragraphs are reproduced herein:
T. Srisailam vs T. Kumar And Another on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174586997/
3 "8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The percentage of permanent disability is expressed by the Doctors with reference to the whole body, or more often than not, with reference to a particular limb.

When a disability certificate states that the injured has suffered permanent disability to an extent of 45% of the left lower limb, it is not the same as 45% permanent disability with reference to the whole body.

The extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) expressed in terms of a percentage of the total functions of that limb, obviously cannot be assumed to be the extent of disability of the whole body.

If there is 60%
permanent disability of the 4 Supreme Court Civil Appeal No. 1579 of 2022 vide order dated 23.2.2022 5 Supreme Court Appeal (Civil), 8598-8599 of 2022,
Judgment Dated: Nov 18, 2022.

entities.text: Supreme Court Civil Appeal No. 1579 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: MGP, J Macma_428_2020 right hand and 80% permanent disability of left leg, it does not mean that the extent of permanent disability with reference to the whole body is 140% (that is 80% plus 60%).

If different parts of the body have suffered different percentages of disabilities, the sum total thereof expressed in terms of the permanent disability with reference to the whole body, cannot obviously exceed 100%."

18. In view of the above discussion and also considering the principle laid down in the above said decisions and as the appellant failed to establish that he cannot do any work of any nature in future due to the injuries sustained by him and also taking into consideration the percentage of the disability of the applicant assessed by PW-2 @ 30%, the contention of learned counsel for the applicant that learned Tribunal ought to have assessed the percentage of functional disability of the appellant @ 100% is unsustainable.

19. Now coming to the quantum of compensation, since this Court has fixed the monthly salary of the applicant @ Rs.10,000/-, the quantum of compensation of Rs.2,52,000/- as awarded by the learned Tribunal is required to be modified.
The annual income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.1,20,000/-.

20. Though the claimant has claimed for future prospects, it is to be seen that the claimant, who was examined as PW1, admitted in his cross examination that even after the accident he was MGP, J Macma_428_2020 drawing salary of Rs.12,000/- per month by working in the same post as Village Revenue Officer of Surepally village.
This admission on the part of PW1 makes it clear that there is no change of office or reduction in the earning capacity of the petitioner/claimant.

Furthermore, as per the cross examination of PW2, who has provided the treatment to the petitioner/PW1, the only difficulty faced by the petitioner due to the injuries is that he could not sit, squat or walk properly.
It is to be observed that the courts cannot award compensation for future prospects unless there is reduction in the injured person's future earning capacity due to the disability.
The concept of 'future prospects' is tied to the potential loss of earning capacity resulting from the injury or disability.

If the injuries sustained by the injured do not impair the petitioner's ability to earn in the future, or if his earning capacity remains unchanged despite the disability, the Court is unlikely to consider future prospects for compensation.

The percentage of permanent disability does not directly equate to the percentage of loss of earning capacity and in fact, a thorough evaluation as to how the T. Srisailam vs T. Kumar And Another on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174586997/
4 disability affects the individual's ability to earn

sentences.text: is required.
In the instant case, as stated supra, the earning capacity of the petitioner has not diminished.
In such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for any future prospects.
MGP, J Macma_428_2020 21.

As discussed supra, the annual salary of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.1,20,000/-
(Rs.10,000/- x 12 months).
The disability as assessed by PW2 and as fixed by the Tribunal is 30%.
There is no dispute with regard to the age of the applicant as 42 years.
There is also no dispute with regard to the relevant multiplier as '14'.
Thus, the quantum of compensation towards disability is Rs.5,04,000/- (Rs.1,20,000/- x 14 x 30%).
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,04,000/- as compensation for the disability.
22. The learned Tribunal failed to award any amount towards attendant charges.

As per Ex.A6, the claimant availed medical leave from 12.08.2012 to 23.06.2013 and during the said period, the claimant might have required the support of an attendant to discharge his day to day activities.
Thus, an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards attendant charges.
The learned Tribunal awarded Rs.1,000/- towards transportation charges, which is on lesser side.
Hence, this Court is inclined to award Rs.3,000/- towards transportation charges.

23. Apart from that the above, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,78,000/- towards medical expenses and extra nourishment, Rs.15,000/- towards pain and sufferance, Rs.58,000/- towards MGP, J Macma_428_2020 expenses for removal of implants.
In this regard, this Court is of the view that there is no need to interfere on the said aspects.

24. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation under different heads as under:

sentences.text:
Now coming to fixing the liability on the respondents, the learned Tribunal while considering oral evidence of RWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence under Exs.B1 to B4 and Exs.X1 and X2,
exonerated the respondent No. 2 - Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation on the ground that the driver of the crime vehicle was not having a valid driving licence at the time of accident and observed that respondnt No.1 owner of the crime vehcile alone is liable to statisfy the award.

The learned counsel for MGP, J Macma_428_2020 the Appellant - Petitioner while relying upon decisions in National Insurance Company Limited v. Swaran Singh and others 6, In the decision of Francisca Luiza Rocha (Supra), the Honourable Supreme Court at paragraph Nos. 7 and 8 held as under:
" In the present case the owner of the vehicle did not contest the proceedings to prove and establish that in spite of best efforts the fact that the driver did not have a valid driving licence was not known to him.

entities.text: MGP, J Macma_428_2020 the Appellant - Petitioner while
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Swaran Singh and others 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: What alone stood proved (by the Insurer) was that the driver of the vehicle did not have a valid driving licence on the date of the accident.

As the driver had a licence but validity of the same had expired, we are of the view that the conclusion of the High Court that the said fact, by itself, constitutes a fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance is not correct.

8. On the basis of the aforesaid finding, we will have to hold that the insurance company (M/s. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.) i.e. Respondent No.2 herein would be liable to satisfy the award and thereafter seek recovery, if so advised, from the owner of the vehicle (Mrs. K. Valarmathi) i.e. respondent No.1."
26.

In view of the principle laid down in the above decision of Honourable Supreme Court and also considering the above violations of the terms and conditions of Ex.B1 insurance policy, this court is of the considered opinion that the learned Tribunal intead of exonerating the respondent No.2-Insurance Company completely from the liability ought to have applied the doctrine of 'pay and recovery' to meet the ends of justice.
6 (2004) 3 Supreme Court Cases 297 MGP, J Macma_428_2020 27.

entities.text: 6 (2004) 3 Supreme Court Cases 297 MGP, J Macma_428_2020 27
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above discussion, this Court feels it just and proper to modify the award and decree passed by the learned Tribunal to the extent of above observations.

28. In the result, the Appeal is allowed in part by enhancing the compensation from Rs.5,04,000/-
to Rs.7,63,000/- which shall carry interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till the date of realization payable by the respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and then take steps for recovering the same from the respondent No. 1 - owner of the crime vehicle.
On such deposit, the appellant- petitioner is entitled to withdraw the same without furnishing any security.
However, the appellant-petitioner shall pay the deficit court fee on the enhanced compensation.
There shall be no order as to costs.
